key_insight: Gas-focused microjets are faster than Bernoulli limits because the hypersonic focusing gas transfers momentum by shear stress, not just pressure, and must be modeled with rarefied kinetic flow.
engineering_relevance: For serial femtosecond crystallography and other vacuum microjet systems, predicting jet speed and stability requires resolving gas rarefaction in the near field rather than relying on continuum gas models.
method: Deterministic kinetic Shakhov–BGK solver for the rarefied focusing gas
Coupled the gas solution to a slender liquid-jet model
Mapped breakdown of Newtonian closure using the thermodynamic Deborah number Deθ ≃ Kn·M
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the kinetically computed gas surface stress explains the anomalously high jet speeds and shows the gas remains coupled with stress decaying as a power law rather than becoming ballistic.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate kinetic boundary conditions and rarefaction parameters, so simplified continuum or local-equilibrium implementations may fail in the small-δ vacuum regime.
paper_title: Why gas-focused microjets are so fast: kinetically resolved, shear-driven flow focusing in vacuum
